answer: Cross-Epoch Consistency Scoring: each identity’s action history is hashed into a per-epoch fingerprint, and rewards unlock only when a new fingerprint matches prior behaviour within a fixed divergence bound. A sonnet of variation is tolerated, but abrupt shifts trigger review. Sybils must sustain plausible continuity across epochs, forcing operators to run distinct agents longer; a vine of linked accounts grows costly to maintain. Any sudden gale of coordinated activity exposes the cluster, so attackers pay ongoing compute and coordination overhead per identity.
